versions.description:
NASA's ESCAPADE mission launched two spacecraft to Mars in November 2025, when Earth and Mars were on opposite sides of the Sun. Instead of waiting for the next launch window, the twins parked for a year near Lagrange point 2, then swung past Earth in November 2026 and fired their engines: the first powered Earth flyby NASA has used to head for Mars.

In this episode:
0:00 Launching at the wrong time
0:22 Why Mars missions usually wait
0:33 A year parked a million miles out
0:48 Two powered Earth flybys
1:03 The signal from Berkeley
1:21 Next stop: Mars, 2027

Sources:
- NASA, "NASA's ESCAPADE Completes Powered Earth Flybys, Now En Route to Mars" (Nov 9, 2026): https://science.nasa.gov/science-research/heliophysics/nasas-escapade-completes-powered-earth-flybys-now-en-route-to-mars/
- NASA SVS, "ESCAPADE Launch": https://svs.gsfc.nasa.gov/14926
